content: Swelling, also referred to as edema in medical terminology, is characterized by the enlargement of organs or tissues due to the accumulation of excess fluid within the interstitial spaces. This pathological condition can occur in various parts of the body and is often indicative of underlying medical issues such as inflammation, injury, or systemic diseases. In the field of engineering, swelling refers to the increase in the volume of a material, which typically occurs as a result of the absorption of a solvent. This phenomenon is commonly observed in plastic polymers. Additionally, neutron-induced swelling is a specific type of material expansion caused by exposure to neutron radiation, which can lead to structural changes and degradation in materials subjected to such conditions.
